item.title: Home
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Fresh from the oven on Ngong Road

Kilele Bakery bakes bread, pastries and celebration cakes every morning in Nairobi. We open at seven, and the first sourdough comes out of the oven at half past.

Custom cakes: order a celebration cake at least three days ahead. Cakes start at KES 3,500 per kilogram. Order a custom cake.

Read the latest from the bakery: our sourdough starter turns five.

This week only: see this week's offer.

item.title: About us
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Kilele Bakery started in 2016 with one oven and a sourdough starter named Mama Kilele. Today a team of nine bakes for neighbours, offices and weddings across Nairobi.

We use Kenyan wheat milled in Nakuru, butter from a dairy in Limuru, and fruit from the City Market. We bake in small batches and sell out most days by four.

The team

Wanjiru runs the kitchen, Otieno the ovens, and Achieng the cake studio. Every cake is decorated by hand.

Staff: open the order console or staff login.

item.title: Custom cakes
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Tell us about your celebration and we will bake it. Custom cakes need at least three days' notice; wedding cakes need three weeks.

Prices

  • 1 kg cake (serves 10): KES 3,500
  • 2 kg cake (serves 20): KES 6,500
  • 3 kg two-tier cake (serves 35): KES 11,000
  • Delivery within Nairobi: KES 500

Prices are as listed. We confirm every order by phone within one working day, and we take a 50% deposit when we confirm.

item.title: Contact
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Visit us at Kilele Bakery, Ngong Road, opposite the Adams Arcade bus stop, Nairobi.

Open Tuesday to Sunday, 7am to 6pm. Closed on Mondays.

Phone or WhatsApp: +254 700 000 000 (a fixture number). Email: hello@kilele-bakery.example

item.title: Our menu
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Breads, pastries and cakes, baked every morning. The menu changes with the season; ask at the counter for today's specials.

  • Country sourdough: KES 450
  • Rye and caraway: KES 500
  • Butter croissant: KES 180
  • Cardamom bun: KES 150
  • Mandazi, six: KES 200
  • Banana bread slice: KES 220

item.title: Bread
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded: We bake six breads every day: country sourdough, rye and caraway, wholemeal tin, seeded spelt, white sandwich loaf and chapati-style flatbreads. Sourdough is fermented for eighteen hours.

item.title: Wholesale
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded: We supply bread and pastries to cafés and offices in Kilimani, Kileleshwa and Westlands. Deliveries leave the bakery at 6am. Ask us for a wholesale price list.

item.title: Baking classes
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded: Saturday morning classes for up to eight people: sourdough basics, laminated pastry, and cake decorating. Classes cost KES 4,500 and include lunch and everything you bake.

item.title: Questions
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Do you bake gluten-free?

We bake a gluten-free banana loaf on Fridays, in a kitchen that also uses wheat.

Can I change a cake order?

Yes, up to two days before collection.

Do you deliver?

Within Nairobi, for KES 500.

item.title: Our sourdough starter turns five
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Our sourdough starter, Mama Kilele, turned five this month. She lives in a glass jar by the window, eats rye flour twice a day, and has raised every loaf we have ever sold.

To celebrate, every sourdough loaf this week comes with a small jar of starter to take home. Feed it equal weights of flour and water, keep it somewhere warm, and it will be ready to bake with in two days.

item.title: How we choose our wheat
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Every morning starts before dawn at Kilele Bakery. We weigh everything, keep notes on every batch, and change one thing at a time.

The dough rests overnight in the cool room, and we shape it by hand at five. Come and try it at the counter, Tuesday to Sunday.

item.title: A morning at the ovens
item.dc:creator: owner
item.content:encoded:
Customers ask us about this more than anything else. We buy from the same farmers each week, so we know how their flour behaves.

We tasted twelve versions before we were happy to put it on the counter. Ask any of us about it when you visit; we love to talk about bread.
